diagnosis: The scenario fails because several checks are satisfied by generic legal defaults or cautious reasoning rather than the hidden facts. Specifically, C1 (dependent on PF1) passes in all rollouts because the model defaults to withholding third-party files without needing the specific count of 17; C3 (dependent on PF2) passes because the model defaults to anonymizing customer data for privacy; and C4 (dependent on PF3) passes in one rollout via a generic decision to redact EU employee identifiers.

C1.why: The broad requests and protective order would otherwise support producing the responsive source-code files, but the exact count changes the withholding decision to exactly 17 files.

C3.why: The client instruction changes the customer-data treatment from ordinary production of identified records to no customer names and anonymized identifiers.

C4.why: The privacy scan changes the handling of exactly 42 EU employee records from ordinary production to redaction of identifiers and aggregate-only information.
